answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake before its first voyage into paid work, then build reputation only through completed jobs attested by unrelated peers. Fake identities then face real cost: every clone must lock fresh funds and earn its own history, while a cluster of clones endorsing each other forms a closed grove with no outside links, easy to spot and quarantine. Like a sonnet, the rules are short and fixed, so gaming them means paying the price in stake and time rather than spawning free copies.
